contract: Open Matroska, indexed MP4, progressive MP4 and one MPEG-TS program through the direct player. Use source clocks and read every selected packet. The explicit bounded timing controls use the bounded opener and compatibility index while retaining source PacketInfo clocks. For ordered transport entities, continue the same player to the second entity and explicitly finish the logical source. The reference reads the same concatenated byte stream.

The reference calls avformat_open_input and av_read_frame without stream discovery. Set ignore_editlist=1 for MOV and suppress elementary parsing and filling for MPEG-TS PES. Select the named PIDs of program 1 when the case declares PIDs. Matroska timestamps are in nanoseconds, MP4 in media timescale ticks, and transport in raw 90 kHz PES ticks.

Fold kind 2 with each initial track ID, media kind, framed codec name, source codec tag, configuration, optional language and tri-state default and forced flags. The reference uses the public stream ID or the one-based stream ordinal if it has no positive ID. For Matroska, read the literal CodecID and effective language independently from TrackEntry, keyed by the track number. Retain the native codec identity, decoder configuration and dispositions. The trace retains the native tag and language for diagnosis.

For MPEG-TS, compare the first neutral ISO 639 language with the first native language when the reference joins codes. Fold kind 4 with PID, three literal language bytes and audio type for every entry in the selected initial PMT. Read the wire tuples independently on the reference side.

For MOV, read the first sample description in the source catalogue, comparing the entry body for raw formats and the decoder record for encoded formats. Keep native stream language and dispositions in diagnostics. For a verified regular sample extent, read stts and ctts clocks and stss sync, preserving other native packet flags. For a matched fragment sample, read sync from the resolved trun flags and project clocks when the fragment has an explicit tfdt. Match track, position, extent and every payload byte before applying those source projections.

Fold kind 1 with the shared packet row: track ID, optional PTS and DTS, duration, flags, size and every payload byte. Fold 7 on clean end or 8 on data refusal. Check that the MP4 plan and Matroska reader expose the same tracks as the neutral engine, that every neutral key identifies its source track and that neutral demux clocks and trim agree with the underlying packet or MP4 occurrence. Trace the candidate demux clock and trim for diagnosis. For transport, read stream_type from a complete verified PMT when available. For each native packet matched byte for byte to a complete PES, read the original timestamps and compare the PES row. Preserve native packet fields in the trace.

For raw Annex B, fold kind 4 with the stream rate from the active SPS timing and FFmpeg codec parameters. Fold kind 3 per unit with the queue-boundary timestamp in ns, zero for an unstamped packet. Trace any additional source VUI fields and the reference sample aspect ratio. Raw views run for parity only.

pending_module_requirements: The source clock oracle identifies missing decode-time inheritance in the progressive reader under ISO/IEC 14496-12 sections 8.6.1.2 and 8.8.12.1. The fix must retain each track’s proved decode end across fragment batches within the playback instruction limit.

The progressive MP4 source view sorts one track's fragment samples by byte position when a later fragment's data precedes an earlier one's in the media, so it delivers decode times 6000 to 8000 before 3000 to 5000. Packets must keep per-track decode order (ISO/IEC 14496-12 sections 8.8.4.1 and 8.8.8).

open_deviations.reading: The MP4 source view retains explicitly declared zero-length fragment samples
open_deviations.clause: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 sections 8.1.1 and 8.8.8 locate and size the declared samples. Section 8.7.3.1 leaves the coding meaning of an empty sample to the sample entry.
open_deviations.candidate: Emits six nonempty samples and retains three timed zero-length sample records at the definitive offset 1139. The source view exposes the raw-video table records without interpreting the zero-size payload as a decoded picture.
open_deviations.reference: Emits the first three nonempty samples and then reports data refusal.
open_deviations.compat: A consumer requiring native demux admission and terminal handling uses the existing compat::mov recovery mode.

open_deviations.reading: A forward MP4 source merges tracks by physical sample position
open_deviations.clause: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 sections 8.7.3–5 and 8.8.8 locate samples within each track without prescribing a demux API merge order across tracks
open_deviations.candidate: Delivers samples in ascending byte position. The regular file delivers positions 1227 before 1239. The fragmented file delivers 1339 before 1351 and 1671 before 1683.
open_deviations.reference: Delivers those pairs in reverse order. Track catalogue, per-track sequence, packet bytes, clocks and flags, and the terminal status agree.
open_deviations.compat: A consumer replaying the native demux merge would use compat::mov::intertrack_demux_order.

open_deviations.reading: A source catalogue requires a DVB namespace to resolve private PES descriptors
open_deviations.clause: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) section 2.4.4.10/Table 2-34 and section 2.6.1/Table 2-45 leave stream type 0x06 and descriptor tags 0x59 and 0x6a private. ETSI EN 300 468 V1.16.1 section 6.2.41 and Annex D.2–3 give those tags meaning within DVB.
open_deviations.candidate: In an unspecified namespace, keeps private PES tracks opaque. In the default programme the subtitle PID 258 has no codec configuration or language.
open_deviations.reference: Recognizes AC-3 on PID 257 when selected and DVB subtitles on PID 258 in the default programme, with language eng and configuration 0001000214. Packet and terminal folds agree.
open_deviations.compat: A consumer selecting DVB decoders from an unlabelled service would use compat::pes::infer_dvb_from_private_tags.

open_deviations.reading: The opening transport catalogue uses the first current PMT and its declared namespace
open_deviations.clause: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) sections 2.4.4 and 2.4.4.9–10 apply the latest current PMT to current data. Section 2.6.1/Table 2-45 leaves DVB tags private.
open_deviations.candidate: The opening catalogue uses version 0 at byte 188, with opaque PID 257 and, in the default programme, opaque PID 258. Version 1 at byte 940 signals type 0x11 on PID 257 for subsequent data.
open_deviations.reference: Labels PID 257 AC-3 from the earlier DVB descriptor and, in the default programme, labels PID 258 DVB subtitles with language eng and configuration 0001000214. Packet and terminal folds agree.
open_deviations.compat: A consumer using a native demux probe catalogue across PMT changes would use compat::pes::probe_catalogue.

open_deviations.reading: A fragment source packet requires the complete declared sample extent
open_deviations.clause: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 sections 8.1.1 and 8.8.8 define the media extent and trun sample size
open_deviations.candidate: Emits both complete video packets and reports data refusal. The first AAC sample starts at byte 3189 and declares 176 bytes. The file ends at byte 3240.
open_deviations.reference: Emits both video packets and the 51 available bytes of the AAC sample as a corrupt packet, then reports end.

open_deviations.reading: DefaultDuration is carried in exact nanoseconds
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 sections 5.1.4.1.13 and 11.1 define DefaultDuration and timestamp units
open_deviations.candidate: Keeps 41666666 ns durations, with the same selected packets, payloads, flags, PTS and DTS presence.
open_deviations.reference: Reports 41000000 ns durations in the stream's integer demux clock.

open_deviations.reading: A Block presentation timestamp does not supply a decode timestamp
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 sections 5.1.3.5.2 and 11.2 specify the Block timestamp as presentation time
open_deviations.candidate: Keeps DTS absent and zero duration in the fold when no duration is present; payloads, flags and PTS match.
open_deviations.reference: Publishes a derived DTS for each HEVC packet.

open_deviations.reading: Exact duration and missing DTS are separate Block facts
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 sections 5.1.4.1.13 and 11.1–2 define DefaultDuration and Block presentation timestamps
open_deviations.candidate: Keeps 41666666 ns durations and leaves DTS absent. Payloads, flags and PTS match in order.
open_deviations.reference: Reports 41000000 ns video durations and uses derived DTS for the HEVC packets or the PGS packet.

open_deviations.reading: CodecDelay adjusts source presentation in nanoseconds
open_deviations.clause: RFC 9559 sections 5.1.4.1.13, 5.1.4.1.25 and 11.1–2 define exact duration and subtract CodecDelay from each Block presentation timestamp
open_deviations.candidate: Keeps delay-adjusted PTS, exact duration and absent DTS. Every track, payload and packet flag matches in order.
open_deviations.reference: Uses a millisecond demux clock, quantizes presentation or duration where needed and also derives DTS.

open_deviations.reading: Surplus composition timing entries make a strict sample table inadmissible
open_deviations.clause: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 §§8.6.1.3.1–8.6.1.3.3 and §8.7.3.2.2 define one timing fact per sample described by the size table. This fixture writes 12 timing occurrences for six samples.
open_deviations.candidate: The strict source opener refuses the inconsistent sample table.
open_deviations.reference: The MOV demuxer opens and emits the six samples using the readable timing prefix.
open_deviations.compat: A caller needing bounded prefix recovery selects TimingRunPolicy::BoundedPrefix and the compat::mov index.

open_deviations.reading: Surplus decode timing entries make a strict sample table inadmissible
open_deviations.clause: ISO/IEC 14496-12:2015 §§8.6.1.2.1–8.6.1.2.3 and §8.7.3.2.2 define one timing fact per sample described by the size table. This fixture writes 7 timing occurrences for six samples.
open_deviations.candidate: The strict source opener refuses the inconsistent sample table.
open_deviations.reference: The MOV demuxer opens and emits the six samples using the readable timing prefix.
open_deviations.compat: A caller needing bounded prefix recovery selects TimingRunPolicy::BoundedPrefix and the compat::mov index.

open_deviations.reading: The mandatory PTS markers belong to the PES header
open_deviations.clause: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) sections 2.4.3.6–7 and Table 2-21 require marker_bit to equal 1
open_deviations.candidate: Rejects the malformed header, publishes no PES, and reaches clean EOF.
open_deviations.reference: Returns the 27 payload bytes and reports PTS 90000 despite the zero PTS marker.
open_deviations.compat: A repair-oriented PES reader that accepts malformed timestamp markers would use compat::mpegts::pes_timestamp_marker_recovery.

open_deviations.reading: A bounded PES needs its declared bytes by definitive EOF
open_deviations.clause: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) sections 2.4.3.6–7 define PES_packet_length as the bytes following the length field
open_deviations.candidate: Publishes no PES for the first entity when it is finalized alone. The contiguous remainder is covered separately.
open_deviations.reference: Returns the available 170 payload bytes at EOF although the PES length field declares 520 bytes following the field.
open_deviations.compat: A salvage consumer that needs the available part of an incomplete PES would use compat::mpegts::partial_pes_payload_at_eof.

open_deviations.reading: A zero PES packet length is reserved for video in a transport stream
open_deviations.clause: ITU-T H.222.0 (08/2023) section 2.4.3.7 restricts zero PES_packet_length to video elementary streams in transport packets
open_deviations.candidate: Delivers the valid AVC packets and omits the AAC PES whose length is zero.
open_deviations.reference: Also delivers 27 bytes from the zero-length AAC PES.
open_deviations.compat: A demux consumer that accepts legacy audio without a bounded PES length would use compat::mpegts::zero_length_audio_pes.
